entry.title: Minecraft’s latest mob is both adorable and helpful. What’s your favorite Minecraft mob?
entry.summary:
Mojang just announced the return of one of the most helpful mobs Minecraft has ever seen. As of today, you can playtest the Copper Golem and its matching copper tools, letting you experience the joys of chest organization while appreciating its adorableness.
The Copper Golem first appeared during Minecraft's Mob Vote 2021, where it and the Glare lost against the Allay. Forgotten by the community for some time, it's now available in the game as part of a beta testing update in Bedrock Edition, with Java receiving the update sometime in the near future.
The addition of the Copper Golem is arriving alongside copper chests, tools, and armor as part of the Vibrant Visuals update. Copper is now a tier between stone and iron, making it a handy resource to obtain early in a new playthrough before you start farming for iron, diamonds, and Netherite.
The Copper Golem itself also has one main perk: item management. As you toss items into copper chests, it'll take those items and organize them into empty chests or those that have a copy of that resource. In short, if you throw some diamonds into it, the Copper Golem will bring them to any chest that already has diamonds in it. If you don't have a diamond chest, it'll put them into any empty one you have.
Every copper item coming to the Vibrant Visuals update will also oxidize over time, giving you several base decorating options. That way, if you want a bunch of orange chests mixed with green-blue armor and an orange golem, you'll have a chance to customize everything however you'd like.
At the time of writing, the Vibrant Visuals update is only available on Minecraft Bedrock Edition. There's currently no word on when it'll arrive on Java Edition.
What's your favorite Minecraft mob? Are you now a Copper Golem fan, or are you more of a Happy Ghast person? Let us know using the poll below or drop a comment below!

However, Front Mission 3: Remake doesn’t just manage to put me off with its deeply frustrating combat mechanics; it feels like a haphazard and even insultingly bad remake once you start digging a little deeper below the surface. These wanzers move around the battlefield and engage with enemies in melee or ranged combat. Each unit has multiple health bars for different parts. Knock out the legs and their movement speed will slow to a crawl. Knock out an arm and the weapon it holds will be disabled. entry.title: The PowerWash clean ‘em up genre is dead, long live the sci-fi undertaker sim
entry.summary:
You'd think there'd be more video games that are explicitly about clearing away corpses, given how many corpses players produce. Getting rid of bodies is a routine problem for developers, with a variety of crafty or cursory solutions. Horror projects such as Resident Evil sometimes resort to accelerated decomposition, with felled zombies dissolving to maggots in seconds, but in most shooters, it's a question of despawning the victims when you look away. Stealth sims mandate a certain level of respectfulness, albeit by accident: stray cadavers must be carefully interred in random dumpsters or closets before they trigger an alarm. As with a lot of things in games, there are technological concerns here that form a curious warping of practicalities in the world beyond the vidbox. Dead bodies in games absorb computing resources that are needed for the next enemies along. Bodies of actual flesh and bone are a weight, if not a burden upon the dead person's loved ones. The memory has to be freed up, so that it can be used for something else.

entry.title: Cyber Knights: Flashpoint review

entry.title: All aboard! The Last Express is ready for testing!
entry.summary: Paris, July 24, 1914. We are excited to announce that Jordan Mechner's acclaimed real-time adventure The Last Express is now ready for testing in ScummVM! Step into the shoes of Robert Cath, an American doctor on the run from murder charges, as he boards the legendary Orient Express for what would be its final journey before the outbreak of World War I. What makes this adventure game truly unique is its time-based gameplay - the game takes place in real time, and characters move within the train following their own schedules, speaking in their native languages, and living their lives whether you're watching or not. But don't worry... you can always rewind time if you missed anything important! To test this game, you'll need the original version of the game (either from the original hybrid DOS/Windows/Mac CDs or from GOG.com) and a daily development build of ScummVM. Please note that the Gold Edition available from Steam is NOT supported - only the original version is compatible at this time. The engine supports the following languages for the game: English, French, German, Italian, and Spanish. We couldn't locate the Japanese version at the moment, but please contact us if you have it! Grab a daily build, have our testing guidelines handy, and get ready for an incredible journey through history, mystery, and one of the most innovative adventure games of the 1990s — and besides... the Orient Express is such a beautiful train, wouldn't you want to take some screenshots while you're there? >
